# Toonik Guide — the whole guide

> The official user guide of Toonik, the frame-by-frame animation app for Android. Source: https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/

# Getting started

Toonik is a frame-by-frame animation app. You draw a picture, add a new frame, draw it again a
little differently, and when the frames play one after another your drawing moves. Everything in
the app is free, there is no account to create and no ads.

## The home screen

![The home screen with four projects](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/home.webp)

- **Projects** and **Movies** — the two tabs. Swipe left or right to switch.
- **☰ (menu)** — opens the side menu (see below). A pink dot means there is something new to read.
- **🔔 (bell)** — your notifications from Toonik. A number shows how many are unread.
- **Pink circle (top right)** — opens Settings.
- **Bottom bar** — **Home**, **Objects** (the object library), **+** (new project), **Learn** (short
  animation lessons) and **Settings**.

Tap a project to open it. The small labels on each card show how long the animation is and its
frames per second (fps).

### The side menu

![The side menu](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/home-menu.webp)

**App settings**, **Object library**, **How to animate** (lessons), **What's new** (what each update
brought), **Notifications**, **About**, **Rate this app** and **Share Toonik**.

## Create a project

Tap the pink **+** at the bottom.

![New project screen](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/new-project.webp)

1. **Project name** — type a name, or keep "My Animation 1".
2. **Choose background** — the four buttons under the preview:
   - **Presets** — paper, white, grid, lined, dot grid, sky, sunset, night sky, meadow, green
     screen, black and more.
   - **Camera** — take a photo and draw over it.
   - **Gallery** — use a picture from your phone.
   - **Color** — a plain colour (pick a swatch or type a HEX code).

   ![Background presets](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/background-presets.webp)

3. **Choose canvas size** — ready-made sizes for YouTube, YouTube Shorts, Instagram, TikTok,
   stickers and more, or type your own width and height (64 to 2048 pixels).

   ![Canvas sizes](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/canvas-size.webp)

4. **Choose frames per second** — how many drawings play each second. **12 fps** is a good start.
   The bouncing ball shows how fast it will look.

   ![Frames per second](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/fps.webp)

5. Tap **Create project**.

> **Good to know:** the canvas size cannot be changed after the project is created. The name,
> speed and background can be changed any time in **Project settings**.

## Work with your projects

**Long-press** a project to select it. Tap more cards to select several.

![Selecting a project](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/home-select.webp)

The bar at the bottom then lets you:

- ✏️ **Rename** (one project at a time)
- ⧉ **Duplicate** — makes a copy called "… copy"
- **Share / Export project** — saves the whole project as a `.flippa` file you can send, back up or
  open on another phone
- 🗑 **Delete** — asks first, and cannot be undone

Tap **✕** at the top to leave selection mode.

### Sort, import and select

Tap **⋮** next to the tabs.

![Sort and import menu](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/home-sort.webp)

- **Sort by** — Last modified, Name or Date created.
- **Import project** — open a Toonik backup (`.flippa`) or a **FlipaClip project (`.fc`)**. It is
  added as a new project; nothing you already have is replaced. From FlipaClip, the layers and
  drawings come across (layer effects and sound do not).
- **Select** — start selection mode.

### Time-lapse recording

Toonik can record every stroke you draw and turn it into a time-lapse video of your drawing.
Select a project, tap **⋯** at the top, and switch on **Time-Lapse Recording**. Later, use **Share
Time-Lapse** from the same place. Time-lapse videos also appear in the **Movies** tab.

![Project options](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/project-options.webp)

## Your work is saved automatically

Toonik saves while you draw (every 10 seconds by default — you can change this in Settings) and
again when you leave the editor or switch to another app. Your projects stay on your phone; nothing
you draw is uploaded anywhere.

## What's new and notifications

**What's new** (side menu) lists every update and what it changed. The **bell** keeps the latest 15
messages from Toonik, even ones you missed. Tap a message to open its link.

![What's new](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/whats-new.webp)

![Notifications](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/notifications.webp)

---

# The editor

This is where you draw. Here is what every part does.

![The editor](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/editor.webp)

## Top bar

| Button | What it does |
|---|---|
| **✕** | Saves and closes the project |
| **Pink diamond** | Opens the **Object library** to add a ready-made character or one of your saved objects |
| **TIMELINE** | Opens the full timeline (see *Frames and timeline*) |
| **Hide interface** (the square icon) | Hides the bars so you see more of your drawing |
| **Pink share arrow** | **Make movie** — export your animation |
| **⋮** | The project menu: add images, audio, stickers, onion skin, grid, project settings and more |

## The toolbar

The white bar near the top holds your tools: **Brush**, **Eraser**, **Lasso**, **Fill**, one more
tool that changes to the last one you used (Text at first), and **⋯** for the rest (**Text**,
**Smudge**, **Blur**, **Magic cut**, **Eyedropper**).

![More tools](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/more-tools.webp)

You can put the toolbar anywhere:

- **Drag the dotted grip** on its left end to move it.
- **Tap the grip** to turn it between lying flat and standing up.
- **Drop it at the side** of the screen and it stands up along the edge.
- **Drop it down by the frames** and it folds up to just the current tool and an arrow — tap either
  to see every tool in a column. Drag it back up to unfold it.

![Folded toolbar with the tool list open](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/toolbar-collapsed.webp)

## The tool options pill

The pill on the right edge changes with the tool. For the brush it shows **Brush** (choose a brush),
**Size**, **Opacity**, **Color** and **Ruler**.

- **Drag up or down** on a control to change it — a bubble shows the value.
- **Tap or long-press** a control to open all the settings for that tool.
- **Tap Color** to open the colour picker.
- Drag its top grip to move the pill anywhere. Let go near a side and it stands against that side.
  (**Left-handed toolbar** in Settings starts it on the left edge.)
- Let go of it down by the timeline and it folds to its main controls (**Size** and **Color** for the
  brush) and an arrow. Tap the arrow to open the rest upwards, and again to fold them. Drag it back up
  to unfold it.

## The bottom bar

**Audio**, **Image/Video**, **Undo**, **Redo**, **Copy**, **Paste** and **Layer** (the pink number is
the layer you are drawing on). The frames of your animation sit just above it.

- **Copy** copies what you have selected, or the whole layer if nothing is selected.
- **Paste** puts it back as a selection in **the same spot** — handy for carrying a drawing to the
  next frame.

## Gestures on the canvas

| Gesture | Does |
|---|---|
| One finger | Draws with the current tool |
| Two fingers pinch | Zoom in and out |
| Two fingers drag | Move around the canvas |
| Two fingers twist | Rotate the canvas (can be turned off in Settings) |
| Two-finger tap | **Undo** |
| Three-finger tap | **Redo** |
| Any tap while playing | Stops playback |

## Smooth zoom

Zoom in close and your lines stay crisp instead of turning into blurry blocks of pixels. Soft
brushes stay soft. Only how it looks on screen changes — your drawing and your movies are exactly
the same. Needs Android 13 or newer; turn it off in **Settings → Canvas & gestures → Smooth zoom**
if you want to see the real pixels (for pixel art).

![Smooth zoom off and on](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/smooth-zoom-compare.webp)

## Hide interface

Tap the **hide interface** button to see more of your drawing. A small set of controls stays: your
current tool, **Show** (brings everything back), **Copy**, **Paste**, play, the frame numbers and
**Layers**.

![Interface hidden](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/hide-interface.webp)

## The project menu (⋮)

![The project menu](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/stage-menu.webp)

At the top you see the project's size, speed and number of frames. Then:

- **Add image**, **Add video**, **Audio**, **Objects**
- **Make sticker**, **Save as object**, **Frames** (all frames in a grid), **Help & tips**
- **Onion skin** and **Grid** — switch them on or off here; **Edit** changes their settings
- **Project settings** — name, speed, timing, drawing outside the canvas and background
- **Make movie**

## Project settings

![Project settings](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/project-settings.webp)

- **Project name**
- **Frames per second** — the speed of the whole animation (1 to 60)
- **Timing** — hold every drawing for 1, 2 or 3 frames (**On ones / On twos / On threes**)
- **Canvas size** — shown here, but fixed once the project exists
- **Draw outside the canvas** — room around the canvas to draw in, and **Room size** to set how much
  (see *Images, video and objects*)
- **Background** — presets, a colour or a picture
- **Stage background** — the colour around the canvas while you draw (not in your movie)

Tap **✓** to save or **✕** to close without saving.

## Leaving the editor

**✕** or your phone's back button saves and closes. The back button first closes whatever is open
(a menu, a sheet, a selection), so press it again to leave.

---

# Drawing tools and colours

## Brush

Pick **Brush** in the toolbar, then tap **Brush** on the right pill to choose from **41 brushes** in
six groups: Basic (Pen, Pen Soft, Ink, Highlighter, Airbrush, Pixel…), Sketch (Pencil, Crayon,
Calligraphy…), Texture (Spray, Grain, Halftone…), Effect (Gradient, 3D Brush, Candy Cane, Sparkles),
Shape (Dots, Squares, Dash…) and Fun (Sprinkles, Leaves, Hair, Fur). Brushes you make yourself are
at the top, under **My brushes**.

![Brush library](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/brush-library.webp)

Your brush, tool sizes and colours stay as you left them, in every project, even after closing the
app.

Tap a brush to use it, or the **›** next to it to change its settings:

![Brush settings](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/brush-settings.webp)

- **Stabilizer** — smooths out shaky lines. Higher is smoother but follows your finger more slowly.
- **Thickness** — 1 to 200 pixels.
- **Opacity** — how see-through the stroke is.
- **Color** — and for two-colour brushes (Gradient, Candy Cane, Sparkles, Sprinkles, Static) a
  **Second color**.
- **Pressure & advanced** — with a stylus, pressure can change the size and/or opacity.

**Tip:** double-tap the Brush tool to switch the ruler on or off.

### Make your own brush

Tap **New brush** under **My brushes** to open the brush maker. Draw on the paper at the top to try
the brush: every change below is painted again on your own line straight away. Tap **✓** to keep the
brush; it goes into **My brushes** and into your hand. The **›** next to one of your brushes opens it
again to change it.

![Brush maker](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/brush-maker.webp)

- **Name** — what the brush is called in the list.
- **Start from** — ready-made looks to begin with: Ink pen, Sketch pencil, Chisel marker, Soft
  airbrush, Dry brush, Chalk, Splatter, Stars, Twinkles, Hearts, Leaves, Bubbles and Confetti.
- **Tip** — the shape the brush stamps along the line: Round, Soft, Pencil, Chalk, Square, Bristle,
  Splatter, Star, Sparkle, Heart, Leaf, Ring — or **Picture**, any picture from your gallery. A dark
  shape on light paper or a PNG with a see-through background works best; **Paint with the light
  parts** flips a light shape on a dark picture.
  - **Roundness** squashes the tip into a flat nib, **Angle** turns it, and **Turn with the stroke**
    makes it follow the direction you draw in (good for leaves, bristles and calligraphy).
- **Stroke** — **Brush size** and **Color** (the same as in the brush settings), **Spacing** (how far
  apart the stamps are), **Flow** (how strong each stamp is: below 100% they build up where they
  overlap) and **Stamps per step**.
- **Taper** — how the line thins at its **Start** and **End**, and whether it also fades. The end
  thins as you lift your finger, once the length of the line is known.
- **Randomness** — every stamp a little different: **Size**, **Opacity**, **Angle**, **Scatter**
  (away from the line), **Hue** and **Brightness**.
- **Texture** — paper grain the line is pressed through (Pencil, Crayon, Canvas, Grunge, Dots,
  Hatch), with its **Depth** and **Scale**. The grain stays on the paper, like a real pencil.
- **Save as a copy** and **Delete brush** are at the bottom when you change a brush you made.

Your brushes are kept with the app, so every project can use them. Size, opacity, colour and
smoothing still come from the brush settings, the same as for the built-in brushes.

## Eraser

![Eraser with its size outline](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/eraser-outline.webp)

The eraser removes drawing from the current layer only.

- **Size** — 1 to 200 pixels. While you erase, a **circle the size of the eraser** follows your
  finger, so you can see exactly what will go. (You can turn the circle off in **Settings → Drawing
  → Eraser outline**.)
- **Fade** — softens the eraser's edge, so drawings fade out at its rim instead of being cut sharply.
- **Opacity** — lower opacity erases a little at a time.

## Fill

Tap inside a closed shape to fill it with colour.

![Fill tool](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/fill-tool.webp)

- **Threshold** — how different a colour can be from the spot you tap and still get filled. Raise it
  if a fill leaves gaps around the edges.
- **Sample all layers** (in the fill settings) — the lines on every visible layer act as the edge,
  but the colour goes on the current layer. Perfect for colouring under a separate line-art layer.

## Text

Choose **Text** (in **⋯** if you can't see it), then tap where the text should go. Its pill on the
right sets the **Color**, **Size** and **Font** before you start.

![Text tool](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/text-tool.webp)

![Add text](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/text-dialog.webp)

Type your words, pick a **Font** (Sans, Serif, Mono, Cursive, Condensed, Poppins), a **Size**,
**Bold**/**Italic**, the alignment and a **Color**, then tap **Add**. The text appears as a
selection you can move, resize and rotate before you put it down.

## Smudge, Blur, Magic cut and Eyedropper

All four are in the **⋯** card on the toolbar.

- **Smudge** — pushes and blends colours like a finger in wet paint. **Strength** sets how far the
  colour travels.
- **Blur** — softens lines under your stroke.
- **Magic cut** — tap the background around a drawing and it is lifted off in one go, ready to move,
  resize or save as an object. Tap inside a drawing instead to cut out just that shape.
- **Eyedropper** — tap anywhere to pick that colour. You go straight back to the tool you were using.

## The colour picker

Tap **Color** on the right pill.

![Colour wheel](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/color-picker.webp)

- **Top bar:** the eyedropper (pick a colour from your drawing), **+** (add this colour to your
  palette), and the old and new colours — tap the old one to go back to it.
- **Tabs at the bottom:**
  - **Wheel** — hue ring, brightness/saturation in the middle, opacity on the arc. Pinch or
    double-tap the middle to zoom for fine control.
  - **Classic** — a square with sliders.
  - **Harmony** — colours that go together (complementary, triadic and more).
  - **Value** — type exact HEX, HSV or RGB numbers.
  - **Swatch** — your recent colours and palettes.

![Palettes](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/color-swatches.webp)

Toonik comes with palettes (Basic, Sketch, Retro Animation, Neon and more). Tap **New palette** to
make your own (up to 12 colours each). **Long-press a colour to replace it**, and swipe a palette
to rename, duplicate or delete it.

## Ruler and guides

Tap **Ruler** on the pill (or double-tap the Brush tool). A bar appears at the bottom.

![Ruler bar](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/ruler.webp)

- **Line**, **Circ** (circle/oval) and **Box** — draw along a perfect shape. Move and size the guide
  with its pink handles. Tap the active shape again to remove it.
- **Mirr** — mirror: whatever you draw on one side is drawn on the other too.
- **Pers** — perspective guides with 1, 2 or 3 vanishing points (**1PT / 2PT / 3PT**). Strokes that
  start near a guide line follow it. **Grid** shows more or fewer lines. Drag a pink point to move it.
  A point that is off the screen or under the bars waits at the edge with a small arrow towards it:
  drag that one and the point moves with your finger.
- **Lock** — keeps the guides from moving by accident.
- **✕** — closes the ruler.

![Circle and mirror guides](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/ruler-circle-mirror.webp)

![Perspective guides](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/perspective.webp)

---

# Select, move, crop and animate

## Select with the lasso

1. Choose **Lasso** in the toolbar.
2. Draw a loop around what you want. It doesn't have to be neat — Toonik picks up just the drawing
   inside the loop and fits the box tightly around it.
3. The drawing now floats in a box you can change.

**Tip:** double-tap the Lasso tool to select everything on the layer.

![A selection with its handles](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/lasso-box.webp)

## The box

| Part | What to do |
|---|---|
| **Inside the box** | Drag to move it |
| **White round corners** | Drag to make it bigger or smaller (keeps its shape) |
| **White bars on the edges** | Drag to stretch it wider or taller |
| **↻ button below the box** | Drag around to rotate. It clicks into place at every 15° |
| **⋯ button above the box** | More options (see below) |
| **Two fingers on the box** | Pinch to resize and twist to rotate |

**Tap outside the box** to put the drawing down. Press **Back** to cancel and leave everything as it
was.

You can move a selection into the room around the canvas too (see *Images, video and objects*).

## The bar under the box

**Trsf** (move, resize, rotate), **Persp** (drag each corner freely for a perspective look), **Move**
(exact placement, below), **Flip** (left–right), **Flip** (up–down), **Crop**, **Animate** and
**Erase** (delete what is selected).

## Move it exactly

When a finger is not precise enough, tap **Move**. Arrows appear above the bar:

![Moving a selection with the arrows](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/selection-move.webp)

- **Tap an arrow** to move the selection one step, or **hold it** to keep moving.
- **X** and **Y** show where the top left of the box is on the canvas, in pixels.
- The button on the right switches the step between **1 px** and **10 px**.

## The ⋯ menu

![Selection options](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/selection-options.webp)

Choose **Transform** or **Perspective**, **Add to selection** or **Remove from selection**, or
**Crop**, **Flip horizontally**, **Flip vertically** and **Delete**.

### Add to or remove from a selection

Tap **Add to selection** or **Remove from selection** in the ⋯ menu. The box steps aside and the
selection shows as a dotted outline. Now every loop you draw is added to it (**Add**), or cut out of
it (**Remove**) — switch between the two on the bar below. Draw as many loops as you like; pinch to
zoom in for small parts. Tap **Done** (or Back) and the box comes back around everything selected,
ready to move, flip or animate.

## Crop

Trim a picture you added, or anything you selected.

![Crop](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/crop.webp)

- Drag the **corners** and **edges**, or drag inside to move the crop box.
- Pick a shape: **Free**, **1:1**, **4:3**, **3:4**, **16:9** or **9:16**.
- **Trim edges** cuts away empty, see-through margins in one tap.
- **Reset** starts again. **Apply** keeps the cropped part exactly where it was, still selected.

## Animate a selection

Turn the selected drawing into a movement in one go — Toonik draws all the frames for you.

![Animate selection](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/animate.webp)

1. Tap **Animate**.
2. Pick a **Preset** (Move left to right, Bounce, Spin, Grow, Shrink, Fade in, Fade out, Shake,
   Float…), or set it up yourself: choose **Start** or **End**, then set **Position** (drag the S and
   E handles on the preview, or use **X** and **Y**: the slider gets close, **−** and **+** move one
   pixel, and holding them keeps going), **Scale**, **Rotation** and **Opacity**. To place a handle
   precisely, tap the **magnifier** in the corner of the preview for a close-up of it (tap again to
   see the whole stage), or pinch the preview with two fingers; one finger moves around while
   zoomed in.
3. Under **Timing**, choose how many **Frames** it lasts, the **Easing** (Linear, Ease in, Ease out,
   Bounce, Elastic…), how many times to **Repeat**, and **Back and forth**.
4. Tap **Create animation**. The movement is put on a new layer called "Animation".

## Copy to another frame

1. Select the drawing with the lasso.
2. Tap **Copy** in the bottom bar.
3. Go to another frame and tap **Paste**. The copy appears **in the same spot**, still selected, so
   you can nudge it before putting it down.

## Save as an object

Keep a drawing to use again in any project: open **⋮ → Save as object**, choose **Selection**,
**Current layer** or **Animation** (a range of frames), give it a name and tags, and tap **Save
object**. It appears in the Object library.

---

# Frames, onion skin and the timeline

An animation is a row of frames. Each frame is one drawing; played quickly one after another, they
move.

## The frame strip

The thumbnails above the bottom bar are your frames. The current one is in the middle with a pink
border.

- **Tap** a frame to go to it.
- **Drag the strip** (or the pink handle above it) to scrub through the animation. A readout shows
  the current frame, the total and the seconds.
- **Pink +** — adds a new, empty frame after the current one.
- **▶** plays the animation, **⏮ / ⏭** jump to the first and last frame. Tap the screen to stop.

## Frame actions

**Long-press a frame** to open its actions.

![Frame actions](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/frame-actions.webp)

- **Hold** − / + — show this drawing for longer (up to 48 frames) without drawing it again.
- **Duplicate**, **Delete**, **Copy**, **Paste before**, **Paste after**, **Move left**, **Move
  right**, **Share** (as a picture).
- Tap **Done**, or anywhere outside the bar, to close it.

## Onion skin

Onion skin shows faint copies of the frames before and after, so you can line up your next drawing.
It is on for new projects and never shows in your movie.

![Onion skin on the canvas](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/onion-skin-stage.webp)

Change it in **⋮ → Onion skin → Edit**:

![Onion skin settings](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/onion-skin.webp)

- **Colored** — earlier frames red, later frames green.
- **Looping** — the last frame also shows the first, for animations that loop.
- **Frames before / after** — how many neighbours to show (0–10).
- **Transparency before / after** and **Skip frames**.

## Grid

**⋮ → Grid** draws guide lines over the canvas to help with spacing. **Edit** sets the line spacing
and how strong they are. The grid is never in your movie.

## The full timeline

Tap **TIMELINE** at the top for a bigger view of every frame, drawn to scale, with your layers and
audio.

![The timeline](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/timeline.webp)

- **Tap** a frame to go to it.
- **Drag the pink grip** on the edge of the current frame to hold it longer or shorter.
- **Long-press** a frame to select it; keep dragging to move it. Tap more to select several.
- **Pinch** to zoom the timeline.
- The **Hold** card at the bottom left changes the selected frame's hold; the preview on the right
  plays the animation.

![Several frames selected](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/timeline-select.webp)

### Groups and loops

Select some frames and tap **Group**. The group can now be repeated with **Loop** — great for a walk
cycle or a blinking eye that plays several times. **Ungroup** undoes it and **Split** cuts a group
in two.

![A frame group with a loop](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/timeline-group.webp)

The bar at the bottom also has **Undo**, **Redo**, **Select / Deselect**, **Duplicate**, **Copy**,
**Paste**, **Delete** and **Layer**. Tap **TIMELINE** again (or ✕ on the preview) to close it.

## All frames at once

**⋮ → Frames** shows every frame in a grid. Tap one to open it, long-press to select (then
duplicate, delete, copy, paste or share), or long-press and drag to move.

![Frames viewer](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/frames-viewer.webp)

## Speed and timing

- **Frames per second** (Project settings) sets the speed of the whole animation. 12 fps is a good
  start; 24 fps looks like film; 4–8 fps looks choppy on purpose.
- **Timing** — *On twos* holds every drawing for two frames, so you draw half as many for the same
  length. Hold single frames from the frame actions or the timeline.

---

# Layers

Layers are like clear sheets stacked on top of each other. Put the background on one, a character on
another, and you can redraw the character without touching the background. A project can have up to
**15 layers**.

Tap **Layer** in the bottom bar.

![Layers](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/layers.webp)

- The layer at the **top** of the list is drawn on top.
- **Tap** a layer to draw on it. Tap the selected layer's name to rename it.
- **≡ handle** — drag to change the order (or long-press the row and drag).
- **👁 eye** — hide or show the layer.
- **Pink +** — add a new layer.
- **›** — the layer's settings.

**Swipe a layer to the left** for **Lock** (stops any drawing on it), **Merge** (joins it with the
layer below), **Duplicate** and **Delete**.

![Layer actions](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/layer-swipe.webp)

## Layer settings

![Layer settings](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/layer-settings.webp)

- **Name** and **Opacity**.
- **Blending mode** — how the layer mixes with the ones below: Normal, Multiply (great for
  shadows), Screen (light), Overlay, Darken, Lighten, Add, Color Dodge, Color Burn, Hard Light, Soft
  Light, Difference, Exclusion, Hue, Saturation, Color and Luminosity.

  ![Blending modes](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/blend-modes.webp)

- **Alpha lock** — paint only over what is already drawn on this layer. Perfect for shading inside
  the lines.
- **Clipping mask** — show this layer only where the layer below has drawing. Put a pattern or
  shadow layer above a character and clip it.
- **Pixel effect** — turns the layer into chunky pixels (choose the pixel size).
- **Glow** — a soft glow around the drawing, with its own colour, size and strength.
- **Merge down** — joins this layer with the one below. **Undo** brings both back. **Duplicate** and
  **Delete** are here too.

Deleting a layer removes it from **every** frame.

---

# Images, video, objects and drawing outside the canvas

## Add an image or a video

Tap **Image/Video** in the bottom bar.

![Add image or video](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/import-media.webp)

- **Photos** — pick one picture, or several at once (up to 30).
- **Videos** — turn a clip into frames.
- **Photo camera** / **Video camera** — take a photo or record a clip right now.
- **File** — from Google Drive, Downloads or any other app.

One picture lands on the canvas as a selection: move it, resize it, **Crop** it, then tap outside to
put it down.

When you pick **several pictures**, Toonik asks:

- **One per frame** — each picture on a frame of its own. Great for turning photos into a
  stop-motion animation.
- **All on this frame** — side by side on the current frame, to arrange together.

### Importing a video

![Import video](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/video-import.webp)

- Drag the ends of the bar to choose the part of the clip (**Start** and **End**).
- **Import as** — **Animation** (many frames) or **Single frame** (one still picture).
- **Look** — **Original**, **Line art** (turns the video into drawn lines; choose **Clean**,
  **Medium** or **Rich** detail) or **Trace guide** (a faint, locked layer with an empty "Ink" layer
  on top, so you can trace over the video).
- **Timing** — **On ones** or **On twos**.

The video goes on a new layer, starting at the current frame. Long clips make many frames, so pick
just the part you need.

## Draw outside the canvas

New projects have **room around the canvas**: draw a character off-screen and walk it in, or draw a
wide background for a camera move. Only what is inside the canvas ends up in your movie.

![Drawing in the room around the canvas](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/draw-outside.webp)

Zoom out to see how much room there is — the dashed line is its edge:

![Zoomed out](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/draw-outside-zoomed.webp)

Turn it on or off in **⋮ → Project settings → Draw outside the canvas**. Turning it off crops
everything drawn outside the canvas from every frame (you will be asked first).

### Make the room bigger or smaller

While it is on, **Room size** under the switch sets how much room there is, by its width and height:

![Room size](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/room-size.webp)

- Drag **Width** or **Height**, or tap **−** and **+** to move each side by 10 px. **Automatic** goes
  back to the size Toonik picks; **Current** to what you have now.
- The preview shows your drawing staying where it is, the new edge in pink and, in red, anything
  that would be cut off. You are asked before anything is cut.
- Each layer of each frame is one picture this size, so room uses memory: **Memory** shows how much.
  When one side reaches what your device allows, make the other smaller to go further. Phones and
  tablets with more memory get more room.
- Tap **Apply**. Changing the room can't be undone and clears Undo.

## The Object library

Ready-made drawings and animations you can drop into any project, plus everything you save yourself.
Open it from the **pink diamond** in the editor or **Objects** on the home screen.

![Object library](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/object-library.webp)

- **Built-in objects** — walk and run cycles, a bouncing ball, a jumping person, a fox, a flapping
  bird, people and animals seen from the front, back and sides (dog, cat, bird, rabbit, panda, fish),
  trees, bamboo, rocks, clouds, sun, moon, stars, a house, a beach ball and a car.
- **Filters** — All, Static, Animated, Favourites, Built-in. **🔍** searches by name or tag.
- Tap an object for its details, to add it to your **favourites**, or to **duplicate** a built-in one
  so you can change it.

![Object details](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/object-detail.webp)

From the editor the library opens as **Insert object** — tap an object to add it:

![Insert object](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/insert-object.webp)

When you add an object to a project you can:

- **Place** — put one frame of it on the canvas as a selection.

  ![Place an object](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/insert-object-place.webp)

- **Stamp** (animated objects) — draw its whole animation across your frames, repeated as many times
  as you like, on the current layer or a new one.

  ![Stamp an animation](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/insert-object-stamp.webp)

- **Animate** — move it across the canvas with a motion you choose, like *Animate selection*.

### Save your own objects

Select a drawing with the lasso (or use a whole layer, or a range of frames), then **⋮ → Save as
object**. Give it a name and tags so it is easy to find later.

---

# Sound

Tap **Audio** in the bottom bar to open the audio editor.

![Audio editor](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/audio-editor.webp)

- The **preview** at the top shows the frame under the blue playhead.
- **🔊** mutes or unmutes all sound while you work.
- **⏮ ▶ ⏭** — play from here, or jump to the start or end.
- The four buttons on the right: **Sound FX** (opens the sound library), **Voice maker**, **Record
  audio** and **Import audio** (music, or the sound of a video file, from your phone).
- There are **6 tracks**, so sounds can play at the same time. Each track can be muted or locked.
- Your frames run along the bottom, so you can line a sound up with the exact drawing.

New sounds are placed at the playhead. **Drag** a clip to move it, drag its ends to trim it, and
**pinch** to zoom in for precise timing.

## Clip actions

**Long-press a clip** for **Rename**, **Duplicate**, **Split at playhead**, **Volume** and **Delete**.

![Clip actions](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/clip-actions.webp)

## The sound library

**169 sounds, all free to use** in your animations, in themed packs: Toonik basics, Fight, Cartoon &
game, Footsteps & moves, Home & objects, Sci-fi & machines, Clicks & alerts, Music jingles and
Voices (an announcer saying "3, 2, 1, Go!", "You win", "Game over"…).

![Sound library](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/sound-library.webp)

Open a pack, tap **▶** to listen and **+ ADD** to put it on the timeline. Every sound has a short
description of what it sounds like.

![A sound pack](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/sound-pack.webp)

### Searching

Type what you want to hear, in your own words — one word or a whole sentence:

- "door" · "someone slamming the door shut" · "footsteps on snow" · "laser gun" · "a happy win tune"

Hindi words in English letters work too:

- "bada dhamaka" · "darwaza band" · "jeet" · "paisa"

The best matches come first.

![Searching with a sentence](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/sound-search.webp)

![Searching in Hinglish](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/sound-search-hinglish.webp)

The sound packs are by Kenney (kenney.nl) and are public domain, so you can use them in anything you
make, even videos you earn money from.

## Voice maker

Type a line, pick a **Voice** (Normal, Kid, Deep, Squeaky, Sleepy) and a **Language** (English or
Hindi), tap **Preview** to hear it and **Add to timeline**.

![Voice maker](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/voice-maker.webp)

## Record your voice

Tap **Record audio**, allow the microphone the first time, then **hold the button** to record and
release to stop. Switch on **Play animation while recording** to speak in time with your drawings.
Recording starts at the current frame.

![Record audio](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/record-audio.webp)

## Animate to the beat

Turn on **Sound while animating** in **App settings → Sound** (it is off until you do). Then:

- **Each frame's sound plays** as you step to it or drag the frame strip, so you can hear exactly
  where a word or a hit lands.
- A **pink note** sits above every frame a beat falls on — a drum hit, a clap, a plucked note. Put
  your key poses there.
- **The sound wave stays on screen while you play** the animation: the wave going by (already played
  in pink), a dot on every beat, and the playhead in the middle lighting up as a beat passes. The
  wave button in the top bar, next to the diamond, hides or shows it.

![Sound wave while playing](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/sound-wave.webp)

---

# Make a movie, stickers and sharing

## Make a movie

Tap the **pink share arrow** at the top of the editor, or **Make movie** in the **⋮** menu.

![Make movie](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/make-movie.webp)

- **Movie name**
- **Output size** — **Original** (the canvas size), **1080p**, **720p**, **480p**, **Square 1080**,
  **Vertical** (1080 × 1920) or **Custom**.
- **Format**:

  ![Formats](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/movie-format.webp)

  - **MP4** — a video with sound. Best for sharing on YouTube, Instagram, WhatsApp.
  - **GIF** — an animated picture. Can have a see-through background. Choose **Loop forever** and
    **Dithering** (smoother colours).
  - **PNG Sequence** — every frame as a picture in a zip file, for video editing apps.
- **Transparent background** — GIF and PNG only.
- **Watermark** — a small Toonik logo in the corner. Off unless you turn it on.
- **Include audio** — MP4 only, when the project has sound.

Tap **Make movie**. When it is ready you can **Share** it, **Save to gallery**, or tap **Done**.

![Your movie is ready](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/movie-ready.webp)

Your movies are kept in the **Movies** tab on the home screen. Tap one to play it, share it, save it
to your gallery or delete it.

![Movies tab](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/movies.webp)

![Playing a movie](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/movie-player.webp)

## Make a WhatsApp sticker

Open **⋮ → Make sticker**. Your animation becomes an animated WhatsApp sticker.

![Make a sticker](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/make-sticker.webp)

1. Pick up to three **Emoji** — WhatsApp suggests your sticker when someone types one of them.
2. Choose a **Pack**, or type a name to start a new one.
3. Tap **Make sticker**.

Toonik frames the sticker around your drawing, so even a small doodle fills it. Stickers are
512 × 512 and under 500 KB, so long animations may lose some frames.

**WhatsApp needs at least 3 stickers in a pack** before it can be added. Until then the pack says how
many more it needs. When it is ready, tap **Add to WhatsApp**. Packs already in WhatsApp show
**Added**; with WhatsApp Business installed too, you can also **Add to Business**. A pack holds up to
30 stickers.

## Share a single frame

Long-press a frame in the frame strip and tap **Share** to send that drawing as a picture.

## Share or back up a whole project

On the home screen, long-press a project and tap **Export project**. You get a `.flippa` file: send
it to a friend, keep it as a backup, or open it on another phone with **⋮ → Import project**.

---

# Settings

Open **Settings** from the bottom bar, the side menu or the pink circle at the top of the home
screen.

![Settings](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/settings-1.webp)

At the top you can **Rate us** and **Share app**.

## Appearance

- **Theme** — System, Light or Dark.
- **Status bar icons** — Auto (dark or light, whichever shows on the canvas), always dark or always
  light.
- **Hide status bar while drawing** — more room for the canvas. Swipe down from the top to see it for
  a moment.

## Drawing

![Drawing and canvas settings](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/settings-2.webp)

| Setting | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Stylus pressure** | Pressing harder with a pen draws thicker | On |
| **Touch sensitivity** | Soft, Medium or Firm — how hard you need to press | Medium |
| **Minimum pressure** | The lightest a pen stroke can be | 12% |
| **Draw input** | Stylus and touch, or **Stylus only** (fingers then only zoom and move) | Stylus and touch |
| **Stylus hover preview** | Shows the brush or eraser size as a circle while a pen hovers over the screen | Off |
| **Eraser outline** | Shows the eraser's size as a circle while you erase | On |

## Canvas & gestures

| Setting | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Smooth zoom** | Lines stay crisp when you zoom in close (Android 13+). Turn off to see the real pixels | On |
| **Canvas rotation** | Twist with two fingers to rotate the canvas | On |
| **Tap gestures** | Two-finger tap to undo, three-finger tap to redo | On |
| **Haptic feedback** | Small vibrations on some buttons | On |
| **Left-handed toolbar** | Moves the tool options pill to the left edge | Off |
| **Keep screen on** | The screen stays on while a project is open | On |

## Sound

| Setting | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Sound while animating** | Each frame's sound plays as you step through frames, a note marks the frames a beat falls on, and the sound wave stays up while playing (see [Sound](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/sound.md)) | Off |

## Projects

![Project and about settings](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/settings-3.webp)

- **Default FPS** — the speed new projects start with (12 fps).
- **Autosave** — how often your work is saved while you draw: every 5, 10 (default) or 30 seconds,
  every minute or every 2 minutes.

## About

- **Open-source licences** — credits for the parts Toonik is built with, including the sound
  library.
- **Reset settings** — puts every setting back to its default. Your projects and movies are not
  touched.

---

# Tips, shortcuts and questions

## Lessons inside the app

**Learn** (bottom bar on the home screen) has short lessons: frame-by-frame basics, frames per
second, onion skin, layers, lasso and copy-paste, ruler and mirror, audio, making a movie and the
object library. Tap a lesson to open its steps.

![How to animate](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/learn.webp)

In the editor, **⋮ → Help & tips** explains every tool in a sentence or two.

![Help and tips](https://getsettalk.github.io/toonik-docs/screenshots/help-tips.webp)

## Handy shortcuts

- **Double-tap Brush** — ruler on or off.
- **Double-tap Lasso** — select everything on the layer.
- **Two-finger tap** — undo. **Three-finger tap** — redo.
- **Long-press a frame** — hold, duplicate, copy, paste, move, share.
- **Long-press any button** — shows its name.
- **Copy, then Paste on another frame** — the drawing lands in the same spot.

## Keyboard (tablets and phones with a keyboard)

| Key | Does |
|---|---|
| ← / → | Previous / next frame |
| ↑ / ↓ | Layer above / below |
| Space | Play / stop |
| O | Onion skin on / off |
| B | Brush |
| E | Eraser |
| Ctrl + Z | Undo |
| Ctrl + Shift + Z or Ctrl + Y | Redo |

## Questions

**Can I change the canvas size later?**
No — choose it when you create the project. The speed, timing, name and background can change any
time.

**Why can't I add another layer?**
A project can have up to 15 layers. Merge two layers (swipe a layer to the left and tap **Merge**) or delete one
you no longer need.

**My sticker pack has no "Add to WhatsApp" button.**
It does, but it stays faded until the pack has 3 stickers — WhatsApp won't take fewer. Make more
stickers into the same pack.

**Something I moved off the canvas disappeared.**
In a project without room around the canvas, whatever is outside the canvas is cut when you put it
down. Turn on **Project settings → Draw outside the canvas** to have room around it (new projects
have it already).

**Smooth zoom makes no difference on my phone.**
It needs Android 13 or newer, and it only shows when you zoom in close. Check that **Settings →
Smooth zoom** is on.

**Where are my movies?**
In the **Movies** tab of the home screen. Use **Save to gallery** to put a copy in your phone's
gallery.

**How do I move my projects to a new phone?**
Long-press a project → **Export project**, send the `.flippa` file to the new phone, and open it with
**⋮ → Import project**.

**Can I open my FlipaClip projects?**
Yes. Export the project from FlipaClip as a `.fc` file, then in Toonik use **⋮ → Import project**.
The drawings and layers come across.

**Do I need an account? Does anything I draw get uploaded?**
No account is needed, and your drawings stay on your phone. Everything in Toonik is free.
